column1: # The performance history: what each workload costs, beside pinned SQLite 3.53.4.
# Appended by `inillucent-perfhistory`, one row per workload per run, never edited.
# Read the RATIO columns across time. Both arms are measured interleaved in the same
# minute on the same machine, so a machine that got busy moves both and leaves the
# ratio alone; the absolute columns are there to catch the case where both moved.
# A ratio above 1 means inillucent cost less than SQLite.
# The wall and cpu ratios are computed NET OF PROCESS STARTUP: each engine's own
# empty-script time (the two `startup_*_wall_ms` columns) is subtracted first. This
# is not a flattering adjustment, it is a necessary one - starting these two shells
# costs about 70 ms and about 20 ms, which is more than several workloads spend on
# their data, so an unadjusted ratio is mostly a measurement of two linkers. The
# absolute columns are NOT adjusted and still include startup.
# `*_wall_ms` is the median round. `*_cpu_ms` is the mean, because Windows accounts
# processor time in ~15.6 ms units and a median of five short rounds is one of two
# values. `*_peak_mib` is the largest round, because that is what a peak is.
# `machine` is a label, not a hostname: the first eight hex digits of a digest of
# whatever this operating system calls the machine, so two machines get two labels
# and one machine keeps its own across runs, without the name itself being published.
# `INILLUCENT_MACHINE` overrides it when a fleet would rather read `ci-linux-x64`.
# `calibration_ms` is a fixed arithmetic loop timed before the run: it says how fast
# this machine is, so rows from two machines can be compared. `drift` is the same
# loop timed again afterwards, divided by the first - a row whose drift is far from
# 1.000 was taken on a machine that changed under it and should be distrusted.
